newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Arab Bank lifts Amman index higher.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Arab Bank lifts Amman index higher.

text.p: Jordan's bourse rose on Sunday after Arab Bank rallied to its highest level in over five years, fuelled by strong local investor demand, dealers said.

The bank, which accounts for almost a third of total bourse capitalisation, rose a further five dinars to 280 dinars and drove the index up in an otherwise weak market, accounting for over half the day's 885,109 million dinar ($1.24 million) turnover.

Brokers attribute Arab Bank's strong gains since the end of weekly trade last Wednesday to forecasts of strong 1997 profits, expectations of a bonus Arab Bank share offering, and government plans to scrap foreign share ownership ceilings.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.62 percent to 164.29 points even though falling stocks outnumbered gainers.
The index is edging close to a three-year high of 164.35 recorded at the start of June after a sustained wave of foreign buying.

"The Arab Bank is leading the activity of the market and all the other stock are weak," said broker Husam al-Hanbali, adding that demand on the share was generated by local floor traders and institutional investors.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 25 to five on Sunday. A further nine were traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.15 percent to 80.87 points, 3.02 percent down from the start of the year.
